title: BlackRock sold $550 million of these cryptocurrencies on Monday
body: BlackRock’s (NYSE: BLK) spot Bitcoin ( BTC ) and Ethereum ( ETH ) exchange-traded funds ( ETFs ) recorded almost $550 million in combined net outflows on November 2. Specifically, BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for the largest share of withdrawals, recording $405.3 million in net outflows. Bitcoin ETF inflow/outflow chart. Source: CoinGlass Its iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) registered another $138.3 million in withdrawals, while the iShares Staked Ethereum Trust (ETHB) shed $4.6 million. Ethereum ETF inflow/outflow chart. Source: CoinGlass The combined outflows reached $548.2 million, highlighting weakening institutional demand for cryptocurrency investment products. Weakening crypto ETF demand The withdrawals came amid a broader downturn across US-listed cryptocurrency investment products, which recorded approximately $545.3 million in combined net outflows on Monday. Bitcoin ETFs led the withdrawals, recording $398.6 million in net outflows, while Ethereum funds registered another $139.7 million. Together, the two largest cryptocurrency ETF categories accounted for approximately $538.3 million in withdrawals. Monday’s withdrawals extended the broader selling trend, marking the third consecutive day of net outflows. Bitcoin funds shed $739.2 million over the preceding seven days, while Ethereum ETFs recorded approximately $566.7 million in outflows. The withdrawals followed a difficult end to October, as security concerns and weakening market sentiment weighed on cryptocurrency investments. Markets rattled after Binance hack A major source of uncertainty was the $6.3 billion Binance hack reported on October 29, which renewed concerns about centralized exchange security. After Binance restored withdrawals, users withdrew approximately $4.65 billion against $1.01 billion in deposits within nine and a half hours, resulting in $3.64 billion in net outflows. Bitcoin subsequently fell towards $76,000 before partially recovering. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers, while Binance said it was working to cover the affected assets. The incident added to existing market pressures, with Bitcoin losing approximately 7.3% in October amid wider credit spreads, a stronger US dollar and concerns about the broader cryptocurrency market. Investors are also monitoring upcoming economic and political developments. The November 3 US midterm elections could influence the regulatory outlook for digital assets, while the November 6 nonfarm payrolls report may shape expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions. title: US Treasury Yield Nears 5% as AI Stock Crash and Midterm Election Risks Collide
body: Key takeaways US 10-year Treasury yield approaches 5% before elections AI stock losses expose mounting technology financing risks Congressional election outcomes could reshape bond market expectations The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed toward 5% on November 3 as investors weighed growing concerns about artificial intelligence spending against uncertainty surrounding the US midterm elections. According to Reuters' latest market report , the benchmark yield reached approximately 4.937% during Tuesday's trading, up from around 4.91% on Monday as global equities weakened. The move comes after Treasury yields exceeded 5% in late October, reviving concerns about borrowing costs for companies already committing hundreds of billions of dollars to AI infrastructure. Why Are Treasury Yields Near 5% Again? Bond markets face competing pressures as investors prepare for election results that could reshape fiscal policy, government borrowing and corporate regulation. A Republican sweep could increase expectations for additional spending or tax measures, potentially pushing yields higher if investors anticipate larger federal deficits. Conversely, divided government could reduce expectations for major fiscal changes. However, neither outcome guarantees a particular direction for bond prices. The 10-year yield also remains below the approximately 5.35% reached during October's Treasury selloff , when inflation concerns and government borrowing requirements pressured long-term debt. The latest rebound follows Monday's decline in yields as falling oil prices eased some inflation concerns. AI Stock Crash Creates Another Risk for Bond Markets The Treasury market is becoming increasingly important for investors assessing the sustainability of the AI expansion. Higher government bond yields can increase corporate borrowing costs while reducing the present value of future earnings, a mechanism explored in our analysis of AI stock valuations . Those pressures are particularly significant for companies financing data centers, semiconductor purchases and electricity infrastructure through debt. The recent AI stock correction demonstrated how quickly investors can reassess technology valuations when spending rises faster than expected financial returns. Oracle, Alphabet and other infrastructure-dependent companies now face greater scrutiny over how their expansion plans will be financed. Meanwhile, CoreWeave's elevated bond yields illustrate how credit investors are demanding substantially higher compensation from some leveraged AI businesses. What Happens After the US Midterm Elections? Investors are watching whether Republicans retain control of Congress or Democrats gain one or both chambers. An MSCI market analysis found that Treasury yields have shown no consistent historical pattern around midterm elections, suggesting economic conditions could matter more than election results alone. The Federal Reserve's future interest-rate decisions, inflation data and corporate financing requirements may ultimately prove more important.

title: China finds a new Gulf partner for its digital yuan push after losing Saudi Arabia
body: China unveiled a CBDC cooperation and a 30 billion yuan currency swap memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Oman. The deals reopen inroads for Beijing’s digital yuan to penetrate into the Gulf region as the world’s second largest economy moves on roughly six weeks after news broke that Saudi Arabia had exited its flagship mBridge settlement platform. What deals did China sign with Oman? China and Oman signed multiple deals at a Beijing meeting between Oman’s Central Bank Governor Ahmed bin Jaafar Al Musalmi and People’s Bank of China (PBOC) Governor Pan Gongsheng. Pan Gongsheng, Governor of the People’s Bank of China, met with Ahmed Moussami, Governor of the Central Bank of Oman. Source: PBOC. One of the deals was a swap arrangement based on the Chinese yuan and Omani rial. They also signed a separate MoU to strengthen digital payment and legal digital currency cooperation between both countries. Per the PBOC’s November 3 statement , the five-year swap deal, capped at 30 billion yuan and matched against 1.5 billion Omani rials, will make the monetary cooperation between the agreeing nations more robust. It will also improve the settlement of cross-border digital payments. In its own release , Oman’s Foreign Ministry said it entered into one agreement, signed 14 memoranda of understanding and a cooperation protocol with China. The arrangements broadly covered emergency technology such as artificial intelligence and a health protocol for Omani dried dates. The Oman Investment Authority signed another 23 agreements and partnerships with Chinese institutions. Commerce Minister Anwar bin Hilal Al Jabri told the Oman News Agency that China was the country’s leading trade partner in 2025, accounting for roughly 23.8% of total trade. Bilateral trade reached 9.6 billion Omani rial (approximately $25 billion) during the year. Oman’s leader, Sultan Haitham bin Tarik and President Xi Jinping of China were also in attendance at the Great Hall of the People, witnessing the signing of the currency agreement. Sultan Haitham is the first Omani head of state to visit China since both nations established diplomatic relations in 1978. When did Saudi Arabia leave the Chinese mBridge platform? The Financial Times reported in September that Saudi Arabia’s central bank (SAMA) was no longer a participant in China’s Project mBridge. SAMA joined the cross-border CBDC platform as an observing member under the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) in 2023. Then it stopped participating when it completed its proof of concept on May 13, 2025. The withdrawal, which was not publicly disclosed before the September FT report , was described as according to the project’s original roadmap. Finance professional Matteo Giovannini argued in a South China Morning Post (SCMP) article that the Saudi exit was “practical” as the apex bank was simply shopping for cheaper cross-border payment options, rather than an “ideological” retreat from the US dollar. China’s central bank has positioned mBridge as a lower-cost rival to SWIFT . Notably, the Oman agreements do not mention mBridge or platform membership, so it is not yet clear whether China has found a replacement for Saudi Arabia in the program. Where the digital yuan push stands mBridge remains the clearest vehicle for internationalizing the e-CNY. The platform uses distributed ledger technology to settle cross-border payments directly between central banks, cutting out correspondent banks. As of early 2026, it had processed more than 4,000 transactions worth about $55.5 billion, with the digital yuan accounting for roughly 95% of settlement volume, Reuters reported citing Atlantic Council data. Its remaining participants include the central banks of mainland China, Hong Kong, Thailand and the UAE, with Macau integrating this year. The push lines up with Beijing’s stated policy. In its 2026-2030 reform plan, the PBOC committed to “steadily develop” the digital yuan and widen use of the renminbi in trade and investment abroad, as Cryptopolitan reported . title: Zach Rector Reveals Major Bullish Data Point for XRP. Here’s What It Means
body: Something is shifting in the XRP ecosystem. In a recent post on X, crypto expert Zach Rector highlighted a trend at the Ripple Swell conference that is gaining momentum among developers and builders in the blockchain space. The XRP ledger is attracting talent again, and this time, the conditions are different. Why Developers Left in the First Place Developers abandoned the XRP ledger because of programmability. Despite its remarkable speed , the network lacked smart contracts, automated market makers, and NFT support for years. Builders moved to Ethereum, Solana, and other chains that offered these tools. The XRP ledger fell behind on what Rector called “the programmability stack.” That gap has now closed. The XRP ledger has added smart contracts, AMM functionality, and NFT support. These were not minor additions. They were the missing infrastructure that kept developers away. Bullish data point for $XRP pic.twitter.com/OUQYIWg3tE — Zach Rector (@ZachRector7) November 1, 2026 Developers Are Coming Back in Large Numbers Rector noted at Ripple Swell that builders who left are now returning. He described them as coming back in droves. These are experienced developers who built on other chains and are now choosing to return to the XRP ledger specifically because its programmability features are now available . This is not a small signal. Developer activity is one of the strongest early indicators of ecosystem growth. When builders choose a chain, they bring projects, users, and liquidity with them. The return of developers who already know the XRP ledger suggests confidence in its current direction. Capital is Ready to Deploy The developer trend does not exist in isolation. Rector also pointed to the capital side of the equation. He noted that there is “a lot of money in the XRP ecosystem” and that investors are ready to fund these returning builders. XRP holders are looking to put their assets to work , and the returning developer base gives them a place to do it. This combination of builder activity and available capital is significant. Development without funding stalls. Funding without developers has nowhere to go. Both arriving together creates conditions for sustained ecosystem growth. What This Means for XRP Going Forward Rector presented this as a bullish signal that many observers are overlooking. The Ripple Swell conference gave direct visibility into who is building and why. The XRP ledger now competes on programmability with chains that have held that advantage for years. Builders who already understand the network’s fundamentals are choosing to return rather than continue building elsewhere. Capital in the ecosystem is positioned to support that activity. title: Crypto Industry Spends $176 Million on US Midterms as CLARITY Act Faces an Uncertain Future
body: Key takeaways Crypto groups spent $176 million across 100-plus races Coinbase and Ripple back influential political spending networks CLARITY Act remains stalled after failed Senate vote The cryptocurrency industry has spent approximately $176 million influencing more than 100 US congressional races ahead of November 3's midterm elections, even as its biggest legislative priority, the CLARITY Act, remains stalled in Washington. A Reuters investigation found that Fairshake and affiliated political committees accounted for approximately $150.8 million through October 20, while other cryptocurrency groups contributed another $25 million in election spending. The campaign represents a major escalation in crypto's political influence , with Coinbase, Ripple and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz among the industry's most prominent financial backers. However, the spending has not secured passage of comprehensive federal cryptocurrency legislation. Crypto PACs Spend Millions as CLARITY Act Remains Stalled The industry's political strategy centers on Fairshake, a super political action committee that spent approximately $196 million during the 2024 election cycle. Fairshake says 53 of the 58 candidates it supported during 2026 primaries or special elections won their contests, although those victories do not guarantee favorable legislative outcomes. The spending has also intensified political battles involving candidates skeptical of cryptocurrency regulation proposals. In Ohio, cryptocurrency-linked political groups have spent more than $68 million in the Senate contest between Democrat Sherrod Brown and Republican Jon Husted, according to Reuters. Earlier, Fairshake affiliate Protect Progress committed $1.5 million to oppose Texas Representative Al Green over his positions on cryptocurrency legislation. Why $176 Million Has Not Secured the CLARITY Act The industry's central objective remains establishing clearer federal rules governing cryptocurrency exchanges, digital commodities and the division of authority between the SEC and CFTC. However, the CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate on September 15, when lawmakers rejected a procedural motion by 49 votes to 50. The unsuccessful vote prevented debate from proceeding under the required 60-vote threshold. It was not a final vote on the legislation itself. Disagreements over ethics provisions, financial safeguards and regulatory oversight had already complicated bipartisan negotiations . The industry's preferred legislation would establish a more durable framework than administrative regulations that could potentially change under future presidents. For Ripple, the setback is particularly significant after years spent pursuing regulatory certainty following its prolonged SEC litigation. What US Midterm Elections Mean for Crypto Regulation The November 3 elections could reshape the legislative environment surrounding digital assets, particularly if control of either congressional chamber changes. Fairshake has supported candidates from both parties, although its most expensive Senate interventions have favored Republicans or opposed Democratic candidates. The industry's efforts have also attracted criticism from campaign-finance watchdogs, who argue that enormous corporate expenditures can distort elections and amplify industry influence over policy. Meanwhile, the SEC has continued developing alternative regulatory frameworks even without comprehensive legislation.

title: Ethereum Supply on Exchanges Hits a Decade Low: Is ETH Preparing for a Major Move?
body: The world’s second-largest crypto asset by market cap has had a rough couple of weeks. But its exchange reserves have dropped to around 14.5 million ETH as of November 2, levels last seen in 2016. That’s a sharp decline from the 2020 peak of roughly 35 million, meaning about 20.5 million Ethereum, or 58.6%, has left tracked exchanges, according to CryptoQuant. Supply Shock? Binance is seeing a similar trend, as its reserves fell to 3.08 million ETH, approaching levels last recorded in late 2020. Compared with its 2025 peak of 4.9 million, the exchange has lost around 1.82 million, a 37.1% drop. Binance now holds approximately 21.2% of total exchange reserves, while the remaining 11.42 million ETH sits across other tracked platforms. The decline means there is considerably less ETH readily available for spot selling. Lower exchange reserves don’t guarantee a price increase, but they could ease selling pressure and create more favorable conditions for price appreciation if buying demand picks up. With fewer coins sitting on exchanges, renewed buying could also have a stronger impact on ETH’s price. Crypto Patel said that Ethereum, currently around $2,245, is approaching an important decision zone. The analyst believes current levels offer a good entry opportunity, but the preferred accumulation range is between $1,800 and $1,900, where a Bullish Order Block and Fair Value Gap overlap. The analyst wants to see a liquidity sweep and bullish confirmation before entering. If the setup plays out as expected, their long-term price targets are $2,700, $3,200, $4,400, $6,000, and $10,000. Persistent ETF Outflows But the institutional side of things continues to be gloomy. US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded their worst month since launch, with investors pulling out $1.61 billion in October, according to SoSoValue data. This surpassed the previous record of $1.42 billion in outflows set last November. October was particularly rough, as the funds saw just three days of net inflows. These were October 13, 21, and 23, bringing in only $24.84 million, $14.96 million, and $4.35 million, respectively. The selling pressure also carried into November, with another $139.8 million withdrawn on the 2nd.
